As You Refine Your Search for Your Quantitative Stories, Additional Materials Will Be Available in Reference Section of Library… Course Objectives: Practicing journalists and those aspiring to enter communications professions are becoming aware that requirements for entry are growing. With the ongoing information explosions, the liberally educated professional communicator must function as a filter, an organizer and interpreter of quantitative data as well as one who gathers and delivers facts. This hands-on course responds to the inherent difficulties in public communication in a time of information overload. The course will include these components: 1. Writing, reporting and editing at an advanced level 2. Using the computer as an assistant for your reporting assignments a. finding information b. evaluating and analyzing info rmation both numerically and verbally c. communicating quantitative data in a way that will pierce the babble of information overload and inform those who need and want quantitative information 3. Computer as Communication Tool a. collect b. compute c. compose Reporting, Writing, and Editing At the beginning of the course, students will review news reporting practices and polish interviewing, writing, reporting, and editing skills. Students will be assigned to cover meetings and speeches on and off campus and to interview sources on and off campus. We will work on editing for grammar, punctuation, spelling, syntax, and news style throughout the course. Students will enroll in the Missouri Group’s Free Companion Site where we will stay informed on global and national news, use the research links, and complete weekly AP style exercises. Because this is an advanced course, enterprise will be both expected and rewarded. Although we will discuss possible assignments in class, it is the work of the students reporters in this course to actively search for, find and cover their own stories – by deadline. The Scene 2009 Students will research and report on issues of critical interest to Augsburg, its students and its urban home, the city of Minneapolis.
